text: The paper reports that wrong intermediate answers by the examinee occur in about 80% of cases where the examiner accepted a false claim and in 45% where it rejected a correct claim. The authors note that in most failures the examinee supplied incorrect information, which may indicate it holds a large set of mutually consistent false facts that make inconsistencies hard to detect.
title: Failures arise when the examinee gives consistent wrong answers
